REGULATIONS FOR BACHELOR OF TECHNOLOGY (TEST FIXTURE)
This file is a short paraphrase of the NSUT B.Tech Regulations 2019-I(A), used only by the automated tests
when the real PDF is not available. Clause numbers and page breaks follow the real document.
1. SHORT TITLE AND COMMENCEMENT.......................... 3
11. ATTENDANCE AND DETENTION............................. 17
11. ATTENDANCE AND DETENTION
11.1. Students are expected to attend every lecture, tutorial and practical class scheduled for them.
11.2. A student needs a minimum attendance of 75% of all classes held in a subject, including lectures, tutorials and practicals, up to the MSE/ESE to be eligible to appear in the MSE/ESE of that subject.
11.3. The Dean Academics may relax the minimum attendance by up to 10% for recorded reasons, such as authorised activities or medical reasons. Documents must be given to the HoD within seven days of resuming studies.
11.4. In exceptional cases the Dean Academics may relax attendance by up to a further 5% on the recommendation of a committee of the Dean Student Welfare, Dean of Faculty and HoD.
11.5. Attendance relaxation may be granted at most 2 times during the programme.
11.6. A student whose attendance is below 60% even after the relaxations in 11.3 and 11.4 cannot appear in the MSE/ESE.
11.7. A student not allowed to appear in the ESE for shortage of attendance gets the FD grade and must register for the course again.
12. PROMOTION AND PASSING A COURSE
12.3. There shall be no supplementary examinations. A student who fails a course must register for it again in a later year or in a summer semester.
12.5. A summer semester may be run for backlog courses that have 10 or more registrations.
12.7. To pass a course, a student must score at least 30% marks separately in the ESE of the theory and practical components.
15. RESULT, AWARD OF DEGREE AND MEDALS
15.1. A student is eligible for the B.Tech degree after earning 162 or more credits with a minimum CGPA of 5.00.
15.5. A student who clears all subjects in the first attempt in eight consecutive semesters with a CGPA of 8.00 or above is awarded First Division with Distinction.
15.6. A student who clears all subjects within the maximum duration with a CGPA of at least 6.50 is awarded First Division.
